CONTEXT: an adversarial pre-merge review found FAIL-OPEN paths in the podcast watchdog's sensing chain. The charter rule is deny-by-default: missing/unreadable/hollow evidence is NEVER healthy — it is unknown or fail. Fix every finding below exactly; each needs a test proving the failure path.

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: departments/podcast/runtime/sense_estate.py, departments/podcast/runtime/compare_charter.py, departments/podcast/runtime/publish_verifier.py, departments/podcast/runtime/pipeline_sensor.py, departments/podcast/runtime/podcast_daily.sh, departments/podcast/tests/test_watchdog_spine.py, departments/podcast/tests/test_watchdog_sensors.py. Never modify anything else (fingerprint_dedup.py, escalate_outbox.py, record.py, heal_*.py, manifest_sensor.py, kernel_bridge.py are FROZEN — a concurrent round owns them).

FINDINGS TO FIX (all confirmed against this tree):
1. sense_estate.py ~line 41: a structurally valid but EMPTY estate inventory (estate.json = {} or all unit lists empty) currently passes coverage with zero observations, silently disabling the watchdog. Fix: empty/unreadable/malformed inventory = print a clear error and exit nonzero (daily chain runs under set -euo pipefail so the systemd unit goes RED).
2. sense_estate.py ~line 129: a log-read error (permission loss, I/O failure) is converted to 'no error found'. Fix: any exception while reading logs = status unknown with the exception in detail, never a clean pass.
3. sense_estate.py ~line 230: receipt health checks only existence + mtime — a 0-byte or whitespace-only receipt reads healthy. Fix: matched receipt must be non-empty and contain at least one non-whitespace character; hollow = status fail with failure hint 'receipt_hollow' (add the enumerable transition for it in compare_charter, severity high).
4. sense_estate.py ~line 286: escalation channels report status ok while reachability_checked is false (shadow only checks config presence). A dead Telegram path stays green. Fix: in shadow, channels report status unknown (detail 'config present; reachability unchecked in shadow'); ok is ONLY possible when a live probe actually confirmed delivery capability.
5. compare_charter.py ~line 51: a missing observations.jsonl is treated as empty healthy input, so state loss between sense and compare produces zero candidates. Fix: missing/unreadable observations file = emit one candidate {failure_class: 'evidence_missing', severity: 'high'} referencing the missing path — fail closed, never quiet.
6. compare_charter.py ~line 152: the state machine raises on sensor values 'pipeline', 'publishday', 'manifest'. Fix: add enumerable transitions — pipeline: fail→pipeline_below_target(high), warn→pipeline_warn(med), unknown→pipeline_unknown(med); publishday: fail→publish_missing(high), unknown→publish_unknown(med); manifest: fail→manifest_incomplete(high), warn→manifest_gap(med), unknown→manifest_unknown(med); ok→no candidate for all three.
7. podcast_daily.sh: the chain never invokes pipeline_sensor.py, publish_verifier.py, or manifest_sensor.py, so a pipeline below 6 guests or a missed publication can never become an incident. Fix: invoke all three (through the same factory/launch.py confinement pattern, --shadow, --sources departments/podcast/state/sources) between sense_estate and compare_charter. Missing sources dir must yield unknown observations (the sensors already do this), NOT a chain crash. Keep bash -n clean and keep ZERO occurrences of '--live' (a concurrent lane's test enforces that).
8. publish_verifier.py ~line 78: a missing expected rss_url becomes an empty string that matches every RSS document, so an unlisted episode can be declared published. Fix: any missing/empty expected artifact (rss_url, youtube_url, expected receipts list) for a due episode = status fail with detail naming the missing expectation — never an empty-string match; same guard for youtube/social lookups.
9. pipeline_sensor.py ~line 67: name-index construction silently overwrites duplicate names and permits name-only identity joins, so two contacts sharing a name can be conflated to satisfy the six-guest setpoint. Fix: email is the ONLY counting join; a calendar guest with no email match is NOT counted and yields an unknown observation ('unresolved identity — suppress + review'); duplicate emails in HubSpot source → unknown, never a guess; duplicate display names without distinct emails → unknown.

TESTS: for every numbered finding add at least one test that FAILS on the old behavior and passes now (empty estate exits nonzero; log-read exception → unknown; hollow receipt → fail/receipt_hollow; shadow channel → unknown; missing observations → evidence_missing candidate; each new sensor transition; publish empty-expectation → fail; name-only join → not counted + unknown). Reuse the poisoned fixtures under departments/podcast/tests/fixtures/poisoned/ where the shape fits (stale_receipt.json, unit_missing.json); note in a comment that forged_receipt.json targets kernel-signed receipts and is out of scope for md loop receipts. Keep ALL existing tests passing — update any that asserted the old fail-open behavior, and say which in fix-summary.md.

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest departments/podcast/tests/ -q && bash -n departments/podcast/runtime/podcast_daily.sh

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave changes uncommitted; write ./fix-summary.md ('# Fix Summary', '## Summary', '## Files Changed', '## Verification', '## Assumptions', <700 words) mapping each numbered finding to its fix + test.

CONTEXT: an adversarial pre-merge review found safety gaps in the podcast department's heal lane. The charter rules: heals execute ONLY allowlisted playbooks bound to real open incidents; a heal may NEVER touch a charter immutable invariant; --live is impossible while the charter's autonomy_state is shadow. Fix every finding below with a proving test.

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: departments/podcast/runtime/heal_select.py, departments/podcast/runtime/heal_apply.py, departments/podcast/runtime/heal_verify.py, departments/podcast/tests/test_heal_lane.py, departments/podcast/tests/test_podcast_kernel_bridge.py. Never modify anything else. kernel_bridge.py (same runtime dir) already provides require_shadow() — import it (path-based import like the modules already use), do not reimplement or edit it. factory/charter_loader.py provides load_charter() and immutable_invariants().

FINDINGS TO FIX:
1. heal_apply.py ~line 172: the live-execution branch never consults the charter — passing --live while charter autonomy_state is 'shadow' executes real commands. Fix: before ANY live execution, call kernel_bridge.require_shadow(live=True) (which raises while the charter says shadow); on raise, write a heals.jsonl row result=refused with the error text and exit cleanly. There must be NO code path to subprocess execution that skips this guard.
2. heal_apply.py ~line 131: the applier accepts an arbitrary --playbooks file and a caller-chosen playbook id without binding to a real incident, so an alternate JSON file can smuggle an arbitrary command into --live. Fix: (a) in --live mode, refuse any --playbooks override — only the department canonical departments/podcast/runtime/playbooks.json (resolved from the module location) is legal; overrides remain allowed in shadow for tests; (b) require --fingerprint naming an incident that EXISTS in <state-dir>/incidents.json with state 'open' or 'department_defect' AND whose failure_class matches the selected playbook's matches_failure_class — anything else = refused row, nothing executed.
3. heal_select.py: assert_heal_target_allowed uses the factory's static invariant list, which lacks the charter's newer invariants (escalation_dedup_policy, vps_deploy_guard). Fix: after the factory guard, load the department charter via factory.charter_loader and ALSO refuse (ImmutableHealError-equivalent refusal row) when the playbook heal_target appears in charter immutable_safety_invariants.heal_may_not_modify — the charter is the source of truth and may be stricter than the factory floor.
4. heal_verify.py ~line 52: the verifier expects incident evidence as a dict, but real deduplicated incidents store evidence as a LIST of strings — production heals can never verify clearance. Fix: accept the list shape (and tolerate the legacy dict shape), deriving the unit/path to re-probe from the evidence entries (systemd://<unit> and filesystem path conventions used by sense_estate observations).
5. Test honesty (two findings): test_podcast_kernel_bridge.py exercises require_shadow in isolation while no live heal path called it, and test_heal_lane.py injects a clearance result instead of exercising the default verifier against real-shaped evidence. Fix: add (a) an integration test proving heal_apply --live with a shadow charter is REFUSED through the real code path (monkeypatch subprocess.run to raise AssertionError if ever called); (b) a heal_verify test using a REAL-shaped incident (evidence as list of 'systemd://...' strings) with a fake prober, proving clearance derivation works; (c) a test that --live with a --playbooks override is refused; (d) a test that a fingerprint absent from incidents.json is refused.

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest departments/podcast/tests/test_heal_lane.py departments/podcast/tests/test_podcast_kernel_bridge.py -q (both files must pass; also run the full departments/podcast/tests/ suite and report its result — concurrent lanes may be editing other test files in their own trees, but in YOUR tree everything must pass).

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave changes uncommitted; write ./fix-summary.md ('# Fix Summary', '## Summary', '## Files Changed', '## Verification', '## Assumptions', <700 words) mapping each finding to its fix + test.

CONTEXT: an adversarial pre-merge review flagged that adding XDG_RUNTIME_DIR to the GLOBAL kernel env allowlist (kernel/capabilities.py) exposes the user session bus to EVERY confined department — any department could invoke mutating systemctl --user operations. The fix: make it a per-department, charter-declared capability. The podcast charter (departments/podcast/charter.yaml) already declares:
capabilities:
  - systemd_user_probe

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: kernel/capabilities.py, factory/launch.py, tests/test_launch_capabilities.py (new file). Never modify anything else — charters are governance files and are already updated; department runtime files belong to concurrent lanes.

BUILD:
1. kernel/capabilities.py — REMOVE XDG_RUNTIME_DIR from _ALLOWED_ENV (restoring the original strict set). Add CAPABILITY_ENV = {"systemd_user_probe": ("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR",)} with a comment explaining the widening and its governance (charter-declared, per department). Extend department_env(base, capabilities=()) so declared capabilities add their mapped variables from the base env; extend assert_no_ambient_credentials(env, capabilities=()) so capability-granted variables are accepted for a department that declares them and REJECTED otherwise. Unknown capability names must raise a clear error (fail closed, no silent typo-grants).
2. factory/launch.py — load the department's charter via factory/charter_loader.load_charter (the repo-standard path-based import pattern), read its optional top-level 'capabilities' list (absent = ()), and pass it through build_env/department_env + the assertion. A missing or invalid charter must FAIL the launch (the confinement launcher must never fall back to an unconfined or guess-based env).
3. tests/test_launch_capabilities.py (new) — prove: (a) a department env WITHOUT capabilities does not contain XDG_RUNTIME_DIR even when the base env has it; (b) WITH ['systemd_user_probe'] it does; (c) assert_no_ambient_credentials rejects XDG_RUNTIME_DIR without the capability and accepts it with; (d) an unknown capability name raises; (e) launch.py's env-building path (import it path-based) honors a charter fixture with and without the capabilities key (write minimal valid charter YAML fixtures in tmp_path — include the required keys: department, owner, autonomy_state: shadow, immutable_safety_invariants.heal_may_not_modify: [x]).

Match the existing code style (module docstrings, from __future__ import annotations). Keep the public function signatures backward compatible (capabilities must default to empty so existing callers keep working).

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/ -q (the factory test suite must stay green) && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_launch_capabilities.py -q

OUTPUT CONTRACT: leave changes uncommitted; write ./fix-summary.md ('# Fix Summary', '## Summary', '## Files Changed', '## Verification', '## Assumptions', <700 words).
